shots.description: One entry per shot, echoing the provided hard-cut boundaries.

content_kind.description: What the shot IS. talking_head = one on-screen person speaking. multi_person_dialogue = two+ people conversing on screen. screen_share_slide = a slide, screen recording, chart or document fills the frame. title_card = designed full-frame text/branding card. poster_static = a static poster/key-art/photo held on screen (often with voiceover). action = subject(s) in significant motion. montage = fast-cut b-roll sequence. broll_scenery = scenery/establishing footage with no specific subject.

key_subject.description: The single subject the crop should follow, if any.

position.description: Rough horizontal position. none = no followable subject.

text_elements.description: Burned-in text/graphics visible in this shot. Judge IMPORTANCE, not readability.

importance.description: essential = the viewer must read it (title, subtitle, price, chart label, speaker name). contextual = adds value but the shot works without it. incidental = watermark, channel bug, background signage, decorative type — losing it costs nothing.

persistent.description: True if this element stays on screen across many shots (a watermark/bug), false if it belongs to this shot.

extent.description: Rough horizontal reach. Coarse buckets only.

speakers.description: Who is audibly speaking during this shot, keyed to the diarization labels provided in the prompt, and where they are ON SCREEN (offscreen = narrator / not visible).

watermarks.description: Video-level persistent overlays (channel bugs, watermarks) present through most of the video.
